utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. As noted, we are sitting pursuant to 15 bis. Mr. Karadzic, are you on your own today?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have a case manager, but he is doing his best to provide documents to the Prosecution and to find the numbers of the existing documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The court deputy has an announcement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Directive number 3 which was tendered by the accused last evening was actually not in evidence, so it's not translated, so it will be MFI D1601 and it's 65 ter 06314.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, you have 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Good morning, Excellencies. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since we do not have too much time, I will do my best to finalise this in a nice and efficient manner and I will put as short possible questions as I can.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 05314.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And I believe you have made reference to this document in one of your footnotes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P3035.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3035.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, since you are familiar with this document, right, that it defines the formation of the organisation in terms of command and control of the Army of Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that is correct. And for your information, it is footnote 201 in the second part of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please. I believe we need the next page in the English, item 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that item 4 entitled: "Command and control of operational groups on the front line" is being implemented by the Main Staff of the Army of SR Bosnia and Herzegovina, and that it is directly subordinate to the Presidency of SR Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That is what the document states, and I explained also in my examination that the term "operative groups" is, in fact, used in this document for the course of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the last page in the Serbian so that we can see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this my signature and the earlier stamp of the Republic of Srpska?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Mr. Karadzic signs as the president of the SR BiH Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that in the Law on the Army, operative and, of course, tactical command over the army is the responsibility of the Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, whereby of course the Main Staff is responsible to the Supreme Command -- I mean, the Supreme Command is only introduced in November 1992, but prior to the Supreme Command, the Main Staff is responsible -- the command of the Main Staff is responsible to the president of the SRBiH Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is already in evidence, and then on page 123 of this section which refers to me in part 2 under (c), you said directive number 7 was amended on the 31st of March, 1995, by directive 7(1). Did -- was the Main Staff authorised to amend this directive to adapt it and to convert it into an executive order?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, if we would apply the principles of command and control, the Main Staff would be allowed to do so after the authorisation of the supreme commander. But it would be good to see this amendment to the directive number 7, because maybe a reference is made to an oral order -- another order of the supreme commander in order to explain that indeed the amendment has been made with the authorisation or maybe on the instruction of the supreme commander and the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We don't have time to call it up. I would like to ask you the following in principle: Were the directives forwarded to the Main Staff from the state leadership, and then was it the Main Staff who was implementing it? Or in other words, did they serve as a basis for the Main Staff to form their own executive decisions?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. We have discussed that in my examination, where we have seen, for example, an order by the Drina Corps which implemented actually the tasks that were set in directive number 6 for the Drina Corps. And there are other examples. And this goes down through the chain of command until the lowest-level units in accordance with the principles of single authority and unity of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at D01140.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I owe it to you because I didn't show it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D01140, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Shall we go into private session briefly?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or maybe we shouldn't broadcast this, but I don't think that it is subject to any restrictions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Sometimes it is prudent not to say that a certain document should not be broadcast in public session. I was told this is a document under seal. Is it -- I wanted to check whether it is sufficient not to broadcast this document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D2613.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I owe you that as well in relation to the order of Colonel Andric. It's General Andric now. 1D2613. It is part of S25392, report of the Secretary-General, but our number is -- yes. Can we have the page before this one, please. Let us just see what they are referring to. The last digits of the ERN number should be 544.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think this --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next one then. Perhaps it was typed out in a different way. Can we have the next one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, do you see the top: [In English] "On the basis of the Agreement of 22nd of May ..."? [Interpretation] Do you see that in the preamble they are referring to that meeting?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see that there is a reference to an agreement of 22nd of May, 1992, but I'm -- I'm not familiar with the contents of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a meeting that was held on the 30th of September, but there is a reference to the meeting of the 22nd of May. And now we're moving on to the agreement of the 22nd of May. 551 is the ERN number that I'd like to see now. 551 are the last three digits of the ERN number. A bit further down. These people met. And let us see where. It says that they met in Geneva on the 22nd of May. Two pages further down.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 2.3, let's look at that, and then the fourth paragraph of that, "the displacement ...": [In English] "The displacement of the civilian population shall not be ordered unless the security of the civilians involved or imperative military reasons so demand. Should such displacements have to be carried out, all possible measures shall be taken in order that the civilian population may be received under satisfactory conditions of shelter, hygiene, health, safety, and nutrition." [Interpretation] Do you remember that six days after this, on the 28th of May, Andric included this aspect in his orders?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the order by the then-Colonel Andric spoke about the move of civilians; I mean, Muslim women and children. I don't remember that he explained the conditions or the surrounding conditions or the context in his order, nor that he referred to any agreement that had been concluded in Geneva on the 22nd of May. It may well be that the two are linked, but I can't establish that link. It may also be that there's just a coincidence in timing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why not? From the 8th of April until the 28th of May, why did he not issue that kind of order? We asked that yesterday. It only happened on the 28th of May. How can it be a coincidence? Obviously he received this. He received a copy of this agreement. And he started involving this in his orders. It was only after the 22nd of May. Did you find any similar order of his before the 22nd of May?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I did not find such an agreement prior to the one dated the 28th of May, but that doesn't mean that there may not have been any instructions to --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, come on, don't. We're not interested in your explanation. We're interested in facts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you're not here to argue with the witness. The witness has answered the question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did not answer the question. He's expanding the question. He's trying to harm the Defence. I'm asking him whether he found it or not. I'm asking -- I'm not asking him what it means.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You, sir, have shown that you are partial --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, he said: "It may well be that the two are linked, but I can't establish that link. It may also be that there's just a coincidence in timing." That's his answer, and whether it's credible or not can be debated later on. It's not for you to argue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would just like to state that the Defence sees bias in all of that, but let it be as you had said. Can we have this document admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, Mr. Karadzic put that he sees bias in all of that. If you'd like to comment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, Your Honours, I explained my methodology in the beginning, i.e., during the examination. It's Mr. Karadzic's observation. I think, as you have explained several times, it's up to the Trial Chamber to decide on these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This has to be admitted under seal as well? It should be no problem. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1603, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D30339 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably you need to give the number again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D01339. I was convinced that we had tendered that earlier. 1D01339. Statement on Bosnia at the London Conference. Page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see (d) and (e)? Please take a look at (d) and (e).

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen them, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (E) again. Could you please focus on that, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably the witness needs to see the first page briefly. No, second page, next one. Yes, Mr. Karadzic, what is your question?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have a look at the last page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm fine with the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Theunens, that Douglas Hogg, minister in the foreign office of Great Britain, Radovan Karadzic, and Nikola Koljevic - could you please show us the bottom of the page - signed all of this. And could you please read ii, the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So do you agree that on the 27th of August, 1992, we took the obligation to create centres for refugees, that we would honour the rights of all refugees and persons whose property was destroyed, and that we would return a substantial portion of the territory once the agreement is adopted?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can only say that, indeed, that is what the paper states, what the document states. But, I mean, the whole issue, when you look back at the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina with all these documents and agreements and signatures, is to what extent were they implemented? So I would only be able to answer the question if I could then also analyse reports and other, I mean, information on the degree of implementation of this agreement. Now it is a piece of paper that has been signed and where we can all read what it states, but the actual value should be -- or resides in the degree of implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Once the Dayton Accords were signed, did we return the most valuable parts of, let's say, part of the city of Sarajevo, such as Ilidza, Hadzici, Vogosca, et cetera? Let's just talk about this. Let's forget about everything else. Did we return all these territories?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just would like to emphasise, this is outside the scope of my report, but, indeed, the Bosnian Serbs returned parts of Sarajevo they controlled. And, I mean, one just has to take into account that the overall situation in December -- November/December 1995, especially the, what I would call, strategic position of the Bosnian Serbs was significantly different from the position they enjoyed in August 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, our position in August 1992 was a better and a stronger one, wasn't it? We were at the peak of our military power when we signed this; right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours, and that refers also to the -- again, the comments General Mladic includes when he signs -- indeed, excuse me, the directive for further operations number 2, to say that actually the gains the Bosnian Serbs have made, territorial gains, allow them to negotiate in the position of the stronger; that is footnote 361 in part 2 of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted and regretfully I have to say that I would have needed many more hours for this witness, but that's how it is. I hope that proper weight shall be attributed to some general statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The final document will be admitted as Exhibit D1604. Thank you, Mr. Karadzic. Yes, Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: May I please have P00956, which is the 16th Assembly Session, and e-court pages B/C/S page 16, and in English, page 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, Mr. Karadzic said that the six strategic goals were not military but rather political goals, over the last few days, and that his statement on these six strategic goals at the 16th Assembly Session was solely an expression of the political situation prevailing at the time. I'd like you to look at the discussion that follows the accused's speech at the 16th Assembly Session. And, here, on the screen, we have Miroslav Vjestica, who, as I understand it, is a member of the Assembly from Bosanska Krupa. And I'm referring to the last paragraph in B/C/S and in English, the portion at the beginning that says: "I fully accept all the strategic goals that have been proposed, but with the proviso that they be operationalised and individuals appointed who shall be responsible for the activities related to each individual goal ..." And then I'd like to direct your attention to halfway down the page in English, and this is the next page in B/C/S, where he states: "For a year and a half, we have been preparing in the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa ..." He goes on to explain the make-up -- the ethnic make-up of the municipality, that there are --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Objection to what? She was just showing the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but this contribution that was freely made by one of the delegates is connecting to me. This is his contribution that was entered into the conclusion. This is not something that I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, it goes to the weight. It's not for you to object to this at this moment. Yes, please proceed, Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: I -- yes, Mr. Theunens, I'm referring you to the conversation or the speech on this page, and then moving on to the portion where this Assembly member states: "Thank God, we did get to our borders because we knew that was how we had envisioned them and drawn them, and you, people's deputies, know well that we had said that the right bank of the Una river would be our border ..." He continues on to discuss future operations in Bosanska Otoka, stating that: "In two to three days, we shall mine the bridge in Bosanska Otoka connecting it with Bosanski Novi. This will be done. I guarantee it." And then towards the bottom of the page in English, he states that: "There are no more Muslims in the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa ..." And then at the very end of this page: "Will they have a place to return to? I think it ..." And we have to go to the next page in English, please. "I think it is unlikely after our president told us the happy news that the right bank of the Una is the border." My question for you, Mr. Theunens, is: Does this passage you have just reviewed relate to the issue of whether the accused's speech had military implications at the 16th Assembly Session?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. I mean, it shows that the strategic goals are implemented and have been implemented also -- I mean, on the terrain, including through the use of military means, already prior to the public announcement at the Assembly session.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: If I can call up 65 ter 04197, please. And while this is coming up, it's a document issued by the War Presidency of Bosanska Krupa, dated the 25th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: And, Mr. Theunens, if I could direct your attention to items 2 and 3 of this document. Both are on page 1 of B/C/S, but you will have to go over to page 2 to complete item 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have read the English page, the first English page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this document dates 13 days after the 16th Assembly Session. Are you able to comment on this document and whether it bears any relation to the speeches by Mr. Vjestica or the accused at the 16th Assembly Session?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have to say that the ARK, I mean the Autonomous Region of Krajina, is outside the scope of my report. But I think that the document is very straightforward in a sense that starting with the second page, reasons, number -- the reason number 1 corresponds with the strategic goal number 4, i.e., establishing a border on the Una and also the Neretva, but that's another area. And if we go back to the first page in English, I believe that there is a reference on removing population.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get information as to whom this proposal was sent, who signed it, and whether it was accepted or not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, don't interrupt the witness's evidence while he's speaking.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not the witness. I'm asking. I can't see who it is sent to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please -- I think it's on the monitor on B/C/S page. Yes, please continue, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. So in the second point, a reference is made to "demolishing as many residential and other buildings, including ..." and so on. One could make a link there to the first strategic goal because residents -- I mean, residential area or building is usually inhabited by civilians. But the most obvious link is obviously to the fourth strategic goal, the establishment of a border on the Una.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This document says "proposal," but proposal to what, if you could know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think -- we can see -- the document is drafted by the War Presidency of the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa, and I would say that it's -- I mean, we have to see who signed it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It says to the command of the first --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, that is a unit of a local -- I mean, the local Serb unit in the area there. So the War Presidency sends a proposal to them, and if we go on the second page maybe there is -- there should be a name as to who signed it and what his position was. It seems --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, it's not clear why -- I mean, the English translation seems to be incomplete, but it's signed by Gojko Klickovic, who is president of the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that this document be marked for identification pending full translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI P3150, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Can I please call up D00825, and page 13 in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: While this is coming up, Mr. Theunens, this is the, I'll call it, memoirs of General Milovanovic, who you discussed yesterday with the accused. And in particular, at T17142, the accused told you that the task that Milovanovic got was to protect the people. And I'd like you -- to refer you to the last paragraph in English, and in B/C/S it's the portion just above the subheading (b), starting with the reference to the 12th May 1992 session in Banja Luka, where he writes: "The six strategic (military) objectives of the Serbian people proceeded from this decision ..." And then he discusses how they were implemented and says: "In the realisation of their objectives, the Serbs used no other means except their own armed power and diplomacy." My question is: Does this relate to the issue of whether the accused's statement of the strategic objectives at the 16th Assembly Session had military implications?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, and what General Milovanovic states there, in my view, corresponds with what I have stated earlier and put in my report; that is, that the six strategic goals are the basis for military orders, starting with the directives for further operations, and then the development of subsequent orders throughout the chain of command within the VRS between May 1992 and, say, September 1995. And, of course -- and that was also highlighted earlier, that in addition to the VRS, also the six strategic goals serve as a basis -- I mean, in addition to serving as a basis for military operations, they also serve as a basis for negotiations. And obviously the two are coherent. The goals one tries to achieve by conducting military operations, one can also -- one would also try to achieve them by the use of diplomacy during negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd ask that these -- this page be added to Exhibit D00825. As I understand it, only pages 30 and 31 of this document are currently admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that General Milovanovic was referred to several times, how about admitting it in its entirety, given that it is his?

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you object to it, Mr. Milosevic -- I'm sorry, my apologies, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if it has a prefix D, it means it's been admitted. What I'm interested in is to identify whether this journal was compiled as a contemporaneous document or whether this was written in hindsight. This is our exhibit, and we introduced that as a document reflecting the things that he saw in Bosnia at the time; whereas this is something that was written afterwards, after he has learned about the existence of the strategic goals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Since Milovanovic was referred to in terms of his statement, interview, I think we'll admit this in its entirety. So it has been admitted, but we change the status as having been admitted in its entirety. Yes, Ms. Elliott.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: May I please have P00970, and starting with page 1 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: And while this comes up, Mr. Theunens, this is the 50th Assembly Session which was held on the 16th of April, 1995, and you refer to this Assembly Session at part 2 footnotes 62, 1051, 1052, and 1105. And on page 1 that we're looking at now, I just ask you to confirm that the minutes record that the accused was in attendance at this session.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is stated on the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: And if I can ask if we can go to B/C/S page 18, English page 22, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: And again, I'm dealing with the topic of military awareness of the strategic goals. And what will come up on the screen is part of General Mladic's speech that you have referred to in your report. And this is towards the end of the first paragraph in B/C/S and the end of the fourth paragraph in English, where General Mladic states: "The tasks of the army in this war stem from the known six strategic objectives adopted by our Assembly which have not been carried out to the full due to the lack of material and other support." Mr. Theunens, does this relate to the issue of whether the accused’s statements of the strategic objectives at the 16th Assembly Session had military implications?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, and in my view, this corresponds with my conclusions in my report, whereby I didn't explicitly refer to this observation made by General Mladic at the 50th Assembly Session, but it is consistent with -- also with my conclusions -- or my conclusions are consistent with it. That sounds better.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: And if I can call up P00988, page 87 in the B/C/S and page 68 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: What I'm calling up, Mr. Theunens, is a speech by the accused at the 53rd Session on the 28th of August, 1995. And starting from the -- reading from the bottom of the English here where the accused says: "To tell the truth, there are towns that we've grabbed for ourselves ..." And I'll need the next page in English only, please. And he continues: "... and there were only 30 per cent of us. I can name as many of those as you want, but we cannot give up the towns where we made up 70 per cent. Don't let this get around, but remember how many of us there were in Bratunac, how many in Srebrenica, how many in Visegrad, how many in Rogatica, how many in Vlasenica, in Zvornik, et cetera. Due to the strategic importance, they had to become ours. And no one is practically questioning it any more." And my question is: Can you explain if there's any relation between this passage we've just reviewed and the accused's statement of the strategic objectives at that 16th Assembly Session?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these towns are essential in order to achieve strategic -- a number of the strategic goals. Bratunac, Srebrenica, Visegrad, Rogatica, we refer -- and, actually, also Vlasenica and Zvornik we refer to the goal of eliminating the Drina as a border, i.e., the third strategic goal. And obviously there's always the first strategic goal: Separation of the Serbian people from the other people, that would also be -- is also implemented through the Serbian or Bosnian Serbs taking control over the towns we just identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ELLIOTT
utterances.text: That concludes my re-examination, Your Honour. I just want to make one note, which is that the accused pursued a number of points about peace negotiations in his cross-examination of Mr. Theunens. We have a report in evidence, the Treanor report referred to yesterday, which is directly on point. And the accused did not actually challenge any aspects of the Treanor report that directly contradict many of the assertions he's been making in court over the past few days, which he is required to do under Rule 90(H). We're not proposing to go through any of the documents in this -- in relation to this issue through Mr. Theunens, who's made it clear it's outside the scope of his report, but I just wanted to advise that the Prosecution may bar table documents in relation to this issue. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's deal with Mr. Theunens first. Thank you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that concludes your evidence. Thank you for your coming to The Hague again. Please have a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good-bye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this question that was raised just now at the very end, that is something that we discussed with Mr. Bell, too. He also accepted that I was persuading people to accept a plan, according to which we were losing Drvar with a 100 per cent Serb population. As for challenging, it has to do with the fact that I do not have enough time for these Prosecution witnesses. I'm challenging everything. It is their creation. I'm challenging everything except for direct quotes. It was done poorly and maliciously. It cannot be said now that I'm not challenging any of it. I'm challenging all of it, but I don't have time to expound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As I believe there will be another time that issue will be raised again, we'll deal with it when it arises. There's one further matter the Chamber would like to raise before we adjourn for the recess. I note that we are still seized of the Prosecution notification of the accused's non-compliance with the Trial Chamber's order on selection of cases for DNA analysis and request for further orders filed on 21st of June, this year. With respect to this request, the Defence, the accused, filed its response on 26th of June, 2011. Speaking for myself, I'm not clear as to the meaning of what is contained in paragraphs 8 and 9 in this response, so it is ordered that the Defence -- to clarify what is stated in paras 9 and 8 and elaborate on its basis in a week's time from now, i.e., by Friday, 29th July. And the Prosecution response, if it so wishes, in two weeks' time from the receipt of the filing by the accused, i.e., by 12th of August. And are there any matters to raise before the recess? Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since Mr. Robinson is in Moscow now on Defence business as assigned by me, can we have a slightly longer dead-line? Can we have more time than up until the 29th of July?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This has been dealt with, in my understanding, by Mr. Sladojevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But Mr. Robinson too, to a large extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me check. Then I'll give you three more days, by 3rd of July -- I'm sorry, 3rd of August, that's Wednesday, and then I think Prosecution will have about ten days, by 12th. Would it be plausible -- or by -- very well. Defence is ordered to file it by 3rd of August, and Prosecution is to be responding by 15th of August, Monday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll do our best. The Defence will do its very best to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In short, I didn't understand what it meant and how it is possible, whether it is true, so I'd like to know the basis of such allegation. That's it. And then we'll adjourn for -- until -- we resume at 9.00 on 16th of August. I wish everybody has a restful and refreshing recess, and I take this opportunity to thank again all the assistance by our precious staff members. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of August, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.11 p.m.,
